pairs.evidence: app/_landing/cosmos/engine/paper.ts:2 This context is a pure paint and rasterisation pipeline (paper grain, inks, palette, seeded RNG, a worker job queue). It has no node/edge model, no pan/zoom camera and no pointer manipulation: a search of app/_landing/cosmos for toWorld, setPointerCapture, zoom and onWheel found nothing, and the only 'edges' hits are paper sheet edges (paper.ts, banner.ts), not graph edges.

techniques.evidence: app/_landing/cosmos/engine/layout.ts:3 layout.ts derives fixed screen geometry from W/H and counts. Nothing converts between screen and world space and nothing reads a pointer, so there is no conversion authority to judge.

pairs.subject: canvas-graph
pairs.evidence: packages/ui/src/components/part/FrameCanvas.tsx:126 FrameCanvas ends a drag only on pointerup and has no onPointerCancel or lostpointercapture handler. After a cancelled gesture the `drag` state stays set, so later pointermove events over that layer keep moving it until some pointerup arrives: the 'drag sticks to the cursor' failure that direct-manipulation names.

techniques.evidence: packages/ui/src/components/part/FrameCanvas.tsx:78 Capturing at press on the layer itself (line 72) is correct. But any movement becomes a live move with no screen-space threshold: a 1px jitter on a ~800px frame rounds to 0.1% and up() then emits an onMove edit for what was meant as a click. Cancel and capture-lost exit paths are also missing (pair anchor).

packages/ui/src/components/part/FrameCanvas.tsx:64 No camera, but there is still a mapping. The one inverse (screen px to frame percent) is a single function next to the forward percent styling, reads the live container rect, and guards against zero size.
packages/ui/src/components/part/FrameCanvas.tsx:42 The surface's only collection is positioned layers. There is no edge or connection type, so no anchor geometry, routing or edge economy to judge.

pairs.registryProposal: canvas-graph scopes itself to relationship/topology surfaces, yet its direct-manipulation and 'no camera is not no authority' rules bind just as well to edge-less layer-composition canvases (a percent-positioned frame editor). Saying explicitly whether such surfaces fall under this subject or under drag-drop would stop seats disagreeing on applicability.
